topic.description: natural science studying celestial objects and phenomena in the cosmos
messages: Concept given explicitly by Wikidata QID.

methodology.source: Wikimedia Analytics Pageviews API (per-article and aggregate, daily)
notes: Monthly averages per reported day are the primary layer for trend analysis; daily data is used for spikes and volatility.
Baseline/latest windows: first/last 3 complete months (or first/last ≤28 days for short periods).
Trend: OLS of ln(views+1) over time, linear OLS and Spearman rank correlation; no significance test.
Outliers: robust z-score (MAD) of log residuals from a 29-day rolling median; influence measured by re-running without spike days.
Evidence strength is a rule-based score, not a probability.

annualizedGrowth.method: Trend-implied annual rate from the log-linear monthly fit: (1 + monthly rate)^12 − 1
annualizedGrowth.note: Descriptive rate for the analysed period, not a forecast.

findings: uk — "Астрономія": average daily views 31.1 → 10.5 (-66.4%; first 3 complete months (Sep 2025–Nov 2025) vs last 3 complete months (Jun 2026–Aug 2026)). Trend: down (-9.01% per month, R² 0.6016, Spearman ρ -0.8392; high confidence). Trend persists after removing 2 spike day(s): change -66.4% with vs -68.8% without; trend down in both. Caution: the compared windows cover different seasons, so this change may be seasonal rather than a real shift. Evidence strength: moderate.

pl — "Astronomia": average daily views 78.3 → 30.5 (-61.1%; first 3 complete months (Sep 2025–Nov 2025) vs last 3 complete months (Jun 2026–Aug 2026)). Trend: down (-7.50% per month, R² 0.4719, Spearman ρ -0.8531; moderate confidence). Trend persists after removing 4 spike day(s): change -61.1% with vs -57.6% without; trend down in both. Caution: the compared windows cover different seasons, so this change may be seasonal rather than a real shift. Evidence strength: moderate.

cs — "Astronomie": average daily views 19.4 → 13.1 (-32.2%; first 3 complete months (Sep 2025–Nov 2025) vs last 3 complete months (Jun 2026–Aug 2026)). Trend: down (-3.74% per month, R² 0.6674, Spearman ρ -0.8392; high confidence). Trend persists after removing 2 spike day(s): change -32.2% with vs -36.8% without; trend down in both. Caution: the compared windows cover different seasons, so this change may be seasonal rather than a real shift. Evidence strength: moderate.

limitations: Pageviews count page loads, not unique users; one person can generate many views.
Wikipedia interest is not market demand, purchase intent, revenue potential or willingness to pay.
News, holidays, school terms, media coverage or links from other sites can cause temporary spikes.
Language editions have very different audience sizes; compare relative growth, not only absolute views.
Article quality, length, renaming and search-engine placement differ between languages and affect views.
Days with zero views are omitted by the API and counted as missing unless --missing-as-zero is set.
Only "user" agent traffic is counted by default; Wikimedia bot filtering is heuristic and imperfect.
Metrics are descriptive; no statistical significance test or forecast is performed.
